title: Deeper/broader current peer issue evidence and failure-mode convergence
scope: ACadRust v0.6.4 release claims versus current version-specific reader issue reports
Peer-reported owner-repair and malformed-input failure modes
Crosswalk of external reports to existing libdxfrw owner, record-boundary, and parser-hardening controls
Current ACadSharp ACIS writer release/PR boundary

method.kind: Read-only review of project release pages, issue bodies, pull request, local plan, and local generated test owner
method.limitations: Issue content is reporter-supplied and was not independently reproduced. Client DWG corpora cited in ACadRust issues are private and were not obtained. ACadRust main and pull request pages are mutable; their behavior is not release behavior. The local owner-test source was inspected but not executed during this research pass.

sources.observed: Release notes list record-bounds work and supplied-corpus strict-read results, plus generation-specific ACIS silhouette/inline-surface work. This does not establish universal corpus coverage or independent semantic correctness.

Reporter says 70 of 351 private AC1032 files opened by v0.6.3 fail under v0.6.4, mostly in AcDbMLeaderObjectContextData, and attributes this to record-bound changes exposing decoder over-read/layout disagreement. The report says AutoCAD and ODA read the files; no corpus was accessed.

Reporter says AC1024 AcDbAssocGeomDependency records fail in v0.6.4; v0.6.3 returns malformed-looking values; and a mutable main route opens after converting the records to Unknown, which the DXF writer omits. The issue labels its root-cause account as a hypothesis and does not publish the client samples.

Reporter describes orphaned entities from erased anonymous dimension blocks being moved into model space and becoming phantom geometry. It reports a private 351-file corpus comparison against ODA-converted DXF read by the same DXF reader; the report was not reproduced here.

Reporter describes v0.6.3 malformed-input count/zero-padding behavior and an attacker-sized allocation on a bit-mutated writer-generated file. This is a peer-reported hardening lead, not a local defect or DWG grammar rule.
Reporter describes an out-of-range slice on a malformed header-size field in a bit-mutated writer-generated v0.6.3 DWG. This report was not independently reproduced.
Release notes list an assembly visibility change and do not list ACIS DXF entity writing.
The ACIS dependent-entity writer PR remains open and undeployed; its page describes Region, CadBody, and Solid3D writing work and a dependency on schema/storage changes.
The issue reports silent omission of ACIS-bearing 3DSOLID/REGION entities on an earlier writer route; it does not establish v3.8.0 behavior.

The generated *D999 orphan-child test checks that an explicit dead owner is not re-homed into model space and that a later valid ENTITIES suffix is still consumed. The test was not executed in this research pass.

assessment.peerEvidenceRule: Keep each report attached to its named project revision, format version, operation, and reporter evidence. A private corpus or issue statement is a lead, not a local reproduction or normative format rule.
assessment.lossDispositionRule: Successful read, strict read, recovery read, unknown-object retention, writer emission, and independent semantic acceptance are separate states. Unknown or skipped data is not preserved merely because a document object is returned.
assessment.ownerRule: Do not repair an unresolved explicit owner by synthesizing model-space membership. Preserve the source owner/disposition and continue only when record and graph boundaries are established.
assessment.hostileInputRule: Check frame remainder, checked arithmetic, allocation/work budgets, and cursor progress independently. Do not import peer numeric limits or use zero-fill to hide truncation.
assessment.implementationSpeedRule: Reuse existing local generated test owners; add only the smallest path-specific vector when a local decoder is changed. Use exact-pinned peers only at an existing composed checkpoint for a named unresolved question.
